tagline: Gravel through the red hills, with dinosaur tracks underfoot.
intro: Four miles west of Shell the backway leaves US 14 and heads south on gravel and dirt, climbing through sage-covered plateaus and badlands under the red walls of the Chugwater Formation, then running down the Alkali Road toward Hyattville. Wind has carved hoodoos along the way. There are no towns, stores or gas stations.
The Red Gulch Road was improved in the late 1950s by heavy machinery going to and from oil wells on the Cherry Anticline. Twelve wells were drilled and not enough oil was found. The road stayed.
season: Travel Wyoming advises driving it when it is open and dry, between May and October.

moments.title: Red Gulch Dinosaur Tracksite
moments.text: Found in 1997, these Middle Jurassic footprints, most of them in a stretch dubbed the ballroom, surprised scientists, most of whom had thought the whole basin lay under the Sundance Sea.

moments.title: Chugwater Formation
moments.text: The red walls can be seen for miles, their color the work of iron meeting oxygen in sediment laid down by an inland sea.

moments.title: Alkali Road
moments.text: From the summit junction the Absaroka Mountains near Cody show across the basin, and the Alkali Road, finished in 1897, carried mail over the mountains by wagon, horseback, sled and snowshoe.

practical: Not recommended from November through April, and even light rain can make the road muddy and impassable. In dry weather a high-clearance two-wheel-drive vehicle can manage it, though large vehicles and trailers may want to avoid it.
